TX-2025892-SB5.aiSummary: The bill gives $200 million from the state savings fund to the governor’s disaster programs for federal matching money and other disaster response and recovery needs. It also gives $50 million for local flood warning sirens and gauges in listed counties, and $28 million for grants to improve weather forecasting and flood warnings. If another camp safety bill passes, it also sets aside money for the health department to carry out that law and lets it raise license fees to cover the cost. It took effect immediately.

TX-2025892-SB16.aiSummary: The bill became law and adds new crimes for real property theft and real property fraud, which cover certain theft or fraud tied to land or buildings. It also sets recording rules for some court papers and county records, and it requires restitution, or repayment, for people, title companies, or insurers harmed by these offenses. The law also directs county clerks to send notice to law enforcement if someone says a real estate filing after January 1, 2026, is fraudulent, and it adds steps for inmate-filed liens that may be fake.

TX-2025892-HB4.aiSummary: This law redraws the Texas districts used to elect members of the U.S. House of Representatives. It sets out new district lines for those elections and says one member is elected from each district. It affects Texas voters and the counties and census areas listed in the law. It took effect on September 5, 2025.

TX-2025892-SR54.aiSummary: The Texas Senate resolution recognizes Children's Emergency Relief International on its ribbon-cutting and the dedication of the George M. Cowden Building as its new Austin headquarters. It says the nonprofit helps orphans, vulnerable children, and families in crisis in several countries, and that the new building will house its main work and may also be used by other Austin nonprofit groups. The resolution also honors George M. Cowden and sends best wishes for the ceremony.
